## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahāpajāpatigotamītherīapadāna* (Thi-Ap 17) is an account in the Therīapadāna section of the Apadāna collection belonging to the late sutta stratum of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. It commemorates the life, verse reflections, and passing of the Buddha's foster mother and founder of the bhikkhunī order, Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī. An English translation of the text by Jonathan S. Walters was published in Donald S. Lopez's *Buddhism in Practice* (1995) [Piya Tan 2002/2004]. In modern scholarship on Buddhist iconographic traditions, specific verses from this apadāna (such as verse 138 in the Navanālandā Mahāvihāra edition) have been cited regarding auspicious signs and symbols—including the banner, *vardhamāna*, *vajra*, and goad (*aṅkusa*)—found upon the body, hands, or feet of the Buddha [Skilling, Symbols On The Body Feet Hands Of Buddha].

In comparative literature, SuttaCentral registers a resembling parallel to this text in the Chinese Ekottarika Āgama (EĀ 52.1), along with shared or related materials found in the Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya (*Cīvaravastu*), the *Udānavarga* (chapter 30, *Sukhavarga*), and the Pali *Dutiyadabba Sutta* (Ud 8.10) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus detects extensive internal Pali text reuse across 60 texts, predominantly within the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (which incorporates over 44,000 characters matching this apadāna), the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, and neighboring biographies in the Therīapadāna, including the apadānas of Kisāgotamī, Uppalavaṇṇā, Yasodharā, and Paṭācārā [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments of this text with parallels in the Tibetan *Vinaya-kṣudraka-vastu* and *Udānavarga*, the Sanskrit *Udānavarga de Subaši*, and the Chinese *Dīrgha Āgama* and *Ekottarika Āgama* [DharmaNexus].
